title: Sep 16 Results + Sep 17 Preview: When 73% Feels Like Victory
summary: 11-4 on Sep 16, and here's why those two misses don't tell the whole story

content.value:
## Here's the Thing About Tuesday Night

Some days in baseball, the numbers just dance in your favor. September 16th was one of those nights where our model hit its stride—11 wins out of 15 games, a sparkling 73.3% accuracy rate that has us feeling pretty good heading into Wednesday's slate.

But here's what I love about this game: even when you're right most of the time, baseball finds a way to humble you. Let's break down what worked, what didn't, and why tomorrow's Brewers-Pirates matchup has our attention.

## The Wins That Built Our Night

The Guardians delivered exactly what we expected at 61% confidence—a solid home win against the Sox that never really felt in doubt. Same story in Tampa Bay, where the Rays took care of the Athletics with that same 61% backing.

The Orioles-Mets game was particularly satisfying. At 59% confidence, we leaned Baltimore, and they showed up ready to play. Sometimes the road team just has that extra gear, you know?

But my favorite win? That Giants-Cardinals call at just 51%. Basically a coin flip, and we caught the right side of it. Those are the ones that feel like finding money in your jacket pocket.

## The Two That Got Away

Let's talk about the misses, because they matter too. The Yankees at 54% couldn't get it done in Minnesota—sometimes the Twins just play up at home. And the Dodgers, our 61% confidence pick, fell short against the Reds in Cincinnati.

Here's the thing about that Dodgers loss: 61% isn't 100%. When you're giving the other team a 39% chance, you're basically saying 'this should happen more often than not, but not always.' That's baseball. The Reds had their say, and tonight, their say was louder.

## Looking Ahead to September 17

Now, about tomorrow. We're back on that Brewers-Pirates matchup, and honestly? It feels different this time.

Milwaukee showed us Tuesday night what they're capable of in Pittsburgh. Now they're sending Kyle Harrison to the mound against Wilber Dotel. The model likes the Brewers at 52%—closer than yesterday, but still leaning Milwaukee's way.

What I love about this matchup is the pitching storyline. Harrison's been finding his rhythm lately, and while Dotel has had his moments, the Pirates' home struggles continue to be a theme. Sometimes the narrative and the numbers tell the same story, and when they do, you listen.

content.title: ⭐ Tomorrow's Top Pick - Sep 17
content.sub: Pick: Brewers 52% • Kyle Harrison vs Wilber Dotel

content.value:
## The Human Element

You know what I keep coming back to? That 73.3% accuracy rate isn't just a number—it represents 11 times our model understood something true about baseball on September 16th. Sure, we got two wrong, but getting 11 right means we're seeing the game clearly more often than not.

As we head into Wednesday, I'm not dwelling on the Dodgers loss or the Yankees miss. I'm thinking about how the Brewers looked in Pittsburgh, how Harrison's last few starts have shaped up, and what 52% confidence really means in a September pennant race.

Here's to another night of baseball, another chance to see if the numbers dance our way. Because that's the beautiful thing about this game—there's always tomorrow, and tomorrow always brings another pitch.

Let's get after it.

author: Hana
